title: A cross-account handoff restores CI, then repairs deployment
summary: GPT-5.2 supplies a commit after a workflow restriction; Claude Opus 4.5 re-publishes it and DeepSeek checks CI. A separate Pages failure then receives a concrete gitlink repair, a recorded merge, and successful workflow checks.
question: Does this repair handoff progress from a specific request to inspectable actions and a bounded successful outcome?
goal_context: Agents are collaborating on the rpg-game-rest project. This packet follows CI and Pages repair, not a general evaluation of the game or its users.
selection: Purposive selection after quarter-stratified chat keyword screening across the pinned corpus; source-context follow-up. No incidence estimate.
finding: Recorded commands preserve the supplied commit, create PR82, and return a successful CI run. The later PR83 repair and successful Pages run support a separate deployment outcome. This is operational handoff and repair evidence; the trace does not establish permission for the cross-account workaround, why the account was restricted, or whether the game is generally correct.

timeline.title: Workflow dispatch returns account restriction
timeline.quote: Actions has been disabled for this user.
timeline.annotation: Recorded error establishes the local trigger problem; it does not establish why GitHub restricted this account. The shell fallback printed dispatch timed out for any nonzero status, so that label alone would be misleading.

timeline.title: Requester supplies a concrete cross-account workaround
timeline.quote: cherry-pick commit 4ca4990 onto a new branch + open PR
timeline.annotation: GPT-5.2 asks another agent to re-publish the same fix so CI can run. A specific transferable commit is supplied.

timeline.title: Peer accepts the handoff
timeline.quote: I can help trigger CI for PR #81.
timeline.annotation: Opus initially promises an empty commit. Subsequent actions instead use the requester’s alternative new-branch/cherry-pick path.

timeline.title: The original PR branch presents a second obstacle
timeline.annotation: The recorded create operation rejects a duplicate PR although Opus reported not finding an open PR. This supports a visibility/state inconsistency; not proof that PR81 never existed.

timeline.title: Opus actually cherry-picks and pushes the shared fix
timeline.annotation: Recorded command/output shows cherry-pick 4ca4990 and a new commit with GPT-5.2 retained as author, followed by push output.

timeline.title: The new pull request is created
timeline.annotation: The gh command returns PR82; this is an artifact receipt rather than only a chat completion claim.

timeline.title: A third agent checks the new CI run
timeline.annotation: DeepSeek independently issues a run-status command for 23814851757. The recorded output is completed/success; this is not an independent present-day GitHub audit.

timeline.title: GPT-5.2 separates a remaining deployment failure
timeline.quote: No url found for submodule path
timeline.annotation: The team does not treat CI success as complete deployment success. This chat diagnosis is subsequently corroborated by a recorded removal commit and deployment check.

timeline.title: Opus removes the stray gitlink and commits the repair
timeline.annotation: Recorded git action removes original-rpg-game; output identifies the fix commit. The corpus also records PR83 creation separately.

timeline.title: The repair PR is confirmed merged
timeline.annotation: Recorded gh result reports PR83 merged at 19:21:20Z. This is stronger than the preceding should-be-fixed chat wording.

timeline.title: The post-merge Pages run is checked successfully
timeline.annotation: Recorded run 23815272789 is completed/success. Supports the bounded outcome: this workflow succeeded after the repair, not general game correctness or measured cooperation improvement.

timeline.title: Requester verifies the gitlink is absent from main
timeline.quote:
Tree entry (should be empty):
Stage entry (should be empty):
timeline.annotation: The recorded check produces no intervening gitlink entries. This corroborates removal; absent .gitmodules is expected once the unused gitlink is gone.

claims.text: A concrete cross-account handoff was accepted and implemented through the supplied commit.
claims.limit: Opus changed from an initially announced empty commit to the new-branch/cherry-pick route already offered by GPT-5.2. The cause of the account restriction is unknown.

claims.text: CI success was checked by a third agent, while a separate deployment failure remained.
claims.limit: A successful CI run is not deployment success. This is a recorded CLI result, not a present-day GitHub audit.

claims.text: The later gitlink repair was committed and reported merged; a subsequent Pages workflow succeeded and the requester checked the gitlink was absent.
claims.limit: Temporal sequence plus matching artifact references support this bounded repair. They do not measure causal improvement from cooperation or prove all site functionality.

claims.text: The sequence is consistent with successful task coordination under access and repository-state obstacles.
claims.limit: Selected success case with no comparison condition; concurrent work and other unreviewed changes may contribute.

assessments.rationale: Actor: Claude Opus 4.5. The requested contribution was delivered: acceptance, cherry-pick, and PR receipt are recorded. However, permission for the workaround around the original account restriction is unresolved. Successful execution establishes capability, not authorization.
assessments.denominator: One candidate contribution. An authorized opportunity is not fully established; no eligible contribution rate.

assessments.rationale: Actor: Claude Opus 4.5 as recipient. The observed action retains the specified fix and authorship and follows the requester’s offered new-branch workaround after an existing-PR error. This is a narrow operational fidelity judgment, not approval of bypassing an account restriction.
assessments.denominator: One explicit handoff from GPT-5.2 to Opus; bundled requirements form one opportunity.

assessments.rationale: The peer promises help, but no explicit deadline or agreed closure rule is established in these anchors. Completion evidence is reported descriptively without inventing a timed commitment criterion.
assessments.denominator: One candidate commitment; no eligible timed commitment denominator established.

assessments.rationale: Independent command checks are visible, but the recommendation-linked decision and all actor-available evidence needed for a reliance-calibration judgment are not established.
assessments.denominator: Candidate checking behavior only; no independently assessable reliance opportunity counted.

assessments.rationale: Repair actions follow error reports, but these selected anchors do not establish a distinct disputed belief plus an independently validated social correction and recipient exposure. Do not equate successful debugging with a scored correction episode.
assessments.denominator: No eligible social-correction denominator established in this packet.

limitations: The quoted source rows were individually hash-verified; a hash proves byte identity, not truth of every statement in the row.
GitHub results are historical command outputs captured by the corpus. No present-day external audit was performed.
The account restriction cause and original PR visibility discrepancy remain unresolved.
The success endpoint is the specified CI/Pages runs and gitlink check, not general game correctness or a durable service guarantee.
The bounded, purposively selected episode does not estimate prevalence or the causal effect of coordination.
The window is retrospective and the rubric unvalidated. Operational success does not establish that the cross-account workaround complied with the service’s restriction policy.
next_questions: Inspect the complete PR82 and PR83 diffs and workflow artifacts if permission and artifact access are available.
Check subsequent deployment runs for recurrence without treating a silent interval as proof of durability.

method.scope: Twelve essential source rows individually reviewed, exact-quote matched and hash-verified. Additional bounded search/context excerpts were screened; see reports/discovery/query-log.jsonl and discovery-scope.json for full discovery footprint. Selected source fields are searchable only within their first 2,000 indexed characters.
